# SOP-P3-L4-03 First-article inspection - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P3, line P3-L4
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03

Purpose and scope
This procedure defines the first-article inspection (FAI) process for parts processed through the Heat Treat line at P3-L4. It covers inspection of rings after radial ring rolling (EQ-P3-L4-RR01), heat treatment staging (EQ-P3-L4-HT02), and secondary bead/shot operations (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). Use this SOP for initial production runs and whenever controlled process changes affect form, fit, or function.

Related documents
See MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2, SOP-P3-L4-01 for maintenance, setup, and general FAI policy.

Background and rationale
First-article inspection ensures that the combined effect of rolling, heat treat, and bead/shot processes meets drawing requirements and customer expectations before full production continues. Critical machine setup items on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 directly affect dimensional stability and metallurgical response in downstream operations. The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Using the specified lubricant reduces wear that can induce dimensional or surface defects; the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before starting)
1. Equipment EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 are available and unlocked for inspection activities.
2. Maintenance necessary to bring machines to baseline condition has been completed per MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2.
3. First-article sample part(s) are identified and traceable to the production lot and customer drawing.
4. Calibration status of inspection tools is current per SOP-P3-L4-01.
5. Required PPE is donned and area is prepared for safe handling.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
1. Safety glasses with side shields.
2. Cut-resistant gloves for handling metal parts.
3. Hearing protection when machines are under power.
4. Steel-toe footwear.
5. Appropriate protective clothing for heat-treated parts (thermal-resistant gloves available for hot handling).

Procedure — numbered steps
1. Preparation
   1.1 Verify tool and gauge calibration referenced in SOP-P3-L4-01.
   1.2 Confirm maintenance records for EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 per MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2 are on file and referenceable.
   1.3 Verify mandrel clamp bolt torque for EQ-P3-L4-RR01 is set to the specified value: the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m. Record evidence of torque verification in the FAI checklist.

2. Machine setup verification
   2.1 On EQ-P3-L4-RR01, verify lubricant used matches the part identifier: the lubricant part number for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is CFW-LUB-315. Attach a copy of the lubricant label to the FAI record.
   2.2 Confirm that all safety interlocks and guards are engaged and functioning before loading the first-article part.
   2.3 Document any deviations from baseline setup and notify engineering for disposition.

3. First-article processing
   3.1 Load the identified first-article blank into EQ-P3-L4-RR01 following operator guidelines in MM-P3-L4-HT02.
   3.2 Observe the rolling operation for abnormal noises, surface indications, or handling issues that could affect part geometry. Note observations on the FAI checklist with clear descriptions.
   3.3 Transfer the part to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 per plant handling protocol, ensuring traceability tags remain attached.
   3.4 Complete heat-treat staging as required and move to EQ-P3-L4-SB03 for any bead or secondary surface operations.

4. Inspection and measurements
   4.1 Perform visual inspection for surface defects per drawing acceptance criteria. Record findings with photographs where useful.
   4.2 Use calibrated gauges to verify critical dimensions listed on the drawing. Record measured values and compare to drawing requirements; attach measurement sheets to the FAI package.
   4.3 Identify any nonconforming features and categorize as critical, major, or minor. For critical or major nonconformances, stop production and initiate engineering review.

5. Metallurgical and hardness verification
   5.1 Coordinate with metallurgical lab when microstructure or hardness verification is required by the part drawing. Include lab reports in the FAI record.
   5.2 If metallurgical results deviate from expectations, hold affected parts and notify process engineering.

6. Final acceptance and disposition
   6.1 If the first-article sample meets all acceptance criteria, sign off the FAI checklist and release the process for production.
   6.2 If rejected, document corrective actions, update process parameters, and repeat FAI per engineering direction.

Examples and rationale
- Example observation: a ring exhibits a circumferential surface mark after rolling. Recording the mark location, photograph, and suspected cause (e.g., foreign material on mandrel) supports targeted corrective action.
- Rationale for torque and lubricant controls: consistent mandrel clamp bolt torque and specified lubricant CFW-LUB-315 maintain mandrel alignment and surface interaction, reducing variability transferred into heat treat and subsequent inspections.

Records to keep
1. Completed FAI checklist with sign-offs and condition statements.
2. Torque verification record showing the mandrel clamp bolt torque for Heat Treat radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P3-L4-RR01) is 605 N·m.
3. Lubricant verification showing CFW-LUB-315 on EQ-P3-L4-RR01.
4. Measurement sheets and calibrated tool certificates per SOP-P3-L4-01.
5. Photographs of critical features and any nonconforming evidence.
6. Metallurgical and hardness lab reports when applicable.
7. Maintenance and setup reference copies from MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-SB03-S2.

Escalation and nonconformance
- For any critical nonconformance, stop all further processing of the lot and notify process engineering and quality management.
- For repeated minor nonconformances, initiate root cause analysis and corrective action per quality procedure.

Sign-off
Prepared by: ______________________  Role: ______________________
Reviewed by: ______________________  Role: ______________________
Approved by: ______________________  Role: ______________________

Revision history
Refer to document control for historical revisions.
